newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU finance ministers delay stability pact accord.
newsitem.headline: EU finance ministers delay stability pact accord.

text.p: European Union finance ministers on Monday postponed an accord on a planned stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline in monetary union, but they will meet to try for a deal before next week's summit, a diplomat said.
A second diplomat said the ministers would meet in Dublin on December 12, the day before the summit of European Union leaders starts in the Irish city. "They were very close," the diplomat said.
At issue is a plan to ensure that those countries which enter European monetary union do not relax their resolve to keep budget spending under control once a single currency is created in 1999.
Earlier, the ministers had appeared closer to an agreement after some movement on defining the exceptional economic circumstances under which a country could overspend.
But British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said the 15 EU member nations had nonetheless been unable to find common ground.
"We were quite close to an agreement, but we were not quite able to reach it," he told reporters after the talks broke up.
